messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate params. The user wants forecast for White Plains next week with temperatures in Celsius. We need to find latitude and longitude for White Plains. White Plains likely refers to White Plains, New York. Coordinates approx 41.0535°N, 73.7629°W. So latitude=41.0535, longitude=-73.7629. Use Open-Meteo API. The function signature expects url, headers optional, timeout, params including latitude, longitude, elevation optional. Also allow_redirects, auth, cert, cookies, proxies, stream, verify.

We need to construct the URL. The Open-Meteo API endpoint for forecast: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Query parameters: latitude, longitude, daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min, temperature_2m_mean? Actually we want forecast for next week. We can request daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,temperature_2m_mean. Also timezone=auto. And start_date, end_date? We can use "start_date" as today, "end_date" as next week. But maybe we can just request daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,temperature_2m_mean, and let the API return next 7 days. The API returns 7 days by default? According to docs, default daily returns 7 days. So we can request daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,temperature_2m_mean. Also timezone=America/New_York. Or timezone=auto. Let's set timezone=America/New_York.

So params: latitude=41.0535, longitude=-73.7629, daily="temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,temperature_2m_mean", timezone="America/New_York".

Also we might want to specify "temperature_unit=celsius"? Actually the API returns temperatures in Celsius by default. So no need to specify unit.

Thus we call function requests_get with url "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast", params as above. We'll set headers default. Timeout default 10.0. Others default.
